page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 30 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 3.75 GB of memory per core. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server allocates 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core on a dedicated basis. The processor configuration includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It lacks local storage and bundled GPUs, and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4n-standard-8 demonstrates strong single-core capabilities. It achieves top-tier status in Geekbench single-core performance with a score of 2256.0 and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 15.25 GB/sec. Text processing and single-threaded gzip compression also register in the top percentiles. Multi-core performance, including Geekbench multi-core and stress-ng multi-core, aligns with the middle tier. Memory bandwidth tests show 690.5 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 61.57 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads.

The hardware configuration includes advanced vector and matrix extensions such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX, which support accelerated mathematical and cryptographic operations. This is reflected in the top-tier text generation speed of 352.64 tokens/sec for small 135M LLM models. However, a key tradeoff is visible in larger workloads; text generation for a medium 7B LLM model drops to a weak 7.21 tokens/sec due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. This instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, single-threaded data processing, web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-8 is an x86_64 virtual machine configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 30 GB of RAM, powered by a 2.3 GHz Intel Xeon 8581C processor. Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, it relies on 4 physical cores with hyper-threading and a 260 MB L3 cache. The instance delivers top-tier single-core performance, as evidenced by its Geekbench single-core score of 2256.0 and high single-threaded decompression speeds. It also features Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions, facilitating efficient cryptography and small-scale vector calculations. While multi-core benchmarks and memory bandwidth align with mid-range averages, the server experiences performance degradation on larger workloads like 7B LLM text generation due to the absence of a GPU. It is highly suitable for general-purpose applications, web serving, text processing, and lightweight inference tasks.
